title: Why Are Real Cars Built to Crumple? 🎮 #GTA6 #shorts
description:
In open-world games you can smash into a wall and keep driving. Real cars are designed to wreck themselves on purpose. In a crash your body has to go from full speed to zero, and what hurts is how fast that stop happens. Crumple zones at the front and back fold and absorb energy, stretching the stop so the peak force drops, while a stiff safety cell around the cabin keeps its shape. Seat belts and airbags stretch your own stop a little more. A Mercedes-Benz engineer, Béla Barényi, patented the idea, and it first reached a production car in 1959.

Follow Hidden Mechanics for more everyday engineering, explained in under a minute.
